source_lines.30: Let $B(0,r)\subseteq K\subseteq B(0,R)$ be a closed convex body in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$. In any rotated coordinates set $C=\{y:\exists t,(y,t)\in K\}$ and $h(y)=\min\{t:(y,t)\in K\}$. Then $h$ is convex, finite on $B(0,r)$, and $L=2R/r$-Lipschitz on $B(0,r/2)$. Every interior point of $C$ has a subgradient, and every such subgradient at a point in the interior of this ball has norm at most $L$.
source_lines.34: Finally, let $a\ge0$. If $x=-\|x\|e_n$ receives OUT and $h(y)\ge h(0)+\langle v,y\rangle-a\|y\|-b$ on $C$, then $s=(-v,1)/\|(-v,1)\|$ satisfies $\langle s,z\rangle\ge\langle s,x\rangle-aR-b-2R\varepsilon/r$ for every $z\in K$.
source_lines.53: 1.1 Compactness of $K$ makes each nonempty vertical section compact, so its minimum exists; projection makes $C$ compact and convex. Convex combinations of two minimizing boundary points show convexity of $h$. For $\|y\|\le r$, the inner ball supplies a point at height zero, while the outer ball bounds all heights below by $-R$. Thus $-R\le h(y)\le0$ on that ball. [given, F1, F5, algebra]
source_lines.55: 2.1 More generally on $B(0,d)$, $0<d<r$, let $y,y'$ be distinct and extend the directed line from $y$ through $y'$ by $r-d$ to $p=y'+(r-d)(y'-y)/\|y'-y\|$. Then $p\in B(0,r)$ and convexity on the segment $[y,p]$ gives $h(y')-h(y)\le R\|y'-y\|/(r-d)$. Exchange $y,y'$ and put $d=r/2$ to obtain the Lipschitz claim. [step 1.1, algebra]
source_lines.57: 2.2 The ball $B((y,0),r/2)$ lies in $K$. Its convex hull with $(y,h(y))$ contains a ball of radius $\theta r/2$ about $(y,(1-\theta)h(y))$ for every $0\le\theta\le1$: combine the vertex with every point of that ball. Consequently all heights between $h(y)(1-2\varepsilon/r)$ and $-r/2$ lie in the inward $\varepsilon$-erosion, whenever this interval is nonempty. If $\varepsilon\ge r/2$ the claimed OUT bound is automatic from $h(y)\ge-R$ and $t\le-r/2$. For $0<\varepsilon<r/2$, write $H=-h(y)\le R$. If the interval is empty, then $H(1-2\varepsilon/r)<r/2$, so $H-r/2<2H\varepsilon/r\le2R\varepsilon/r$; every $t\le-r/2$ therefore satisfies $t<h(y)+2R\varepsilon/r$. If the interval is nonempty, OUT excludes its heights, so $t\le h(y)(1-2\varepsilon/r)\le h(y)+2R\varepsilon/r$. This uses an inclusion of balls, not an incorrect identity for the erosion of a cone. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]
source_lines.59: 3.1 For completeness, subgradients here need no arbitrary selection. The truncated epigraph $E=\{(y,t):y\in C,\ h(y)\le t\le R+1\}$ is compact and convex: it is the image of the compact set of pairs consisting of a point of $K$ and a permitted upward vertical displacement. Fix interior $y$ and $p=(y,h(y))$. Let $p_j=p-e_n/j$, and let $q_j$ be its unique nearest point in $E$ by [F2]. Minimality along a segment gives $\langle q_j-p_j,w-q_j\rangle\ge0$ for all $w\in E$, by expanding squared distance and taking the right derivative at zero. Moreover $\|q_j-p\|\le2/j$. A subsequence of the unit normals $(q_j-p_j)/\|q_j-p_j\|$ converges by [F3] to a unit normal $(u,t)$ with $\langle(u,t),w-p\rangle\ge0$ on $E$. Upward vertical segments imply $t\ge0$; if $t=0$, interior displacements of $y$ in both horizontal directions force $u=0$, a contradiction. Thus $t>0$ and $-u/t$ is a subgradient of $h$ on $C$. At a point where the Lipschitz bound holds on a neighborhood, applying the subgradient inequality in the directions $\pm p/\|p\|$ gives $\|p\|\le L$. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]
source_lines.61: 4.1 Fix $\|y\|\le r/2$. A subgradient $p$ of norm at most $2R/r$ gives the supporting inequality $\langle(-p,1),(z,t')-(y,h(y))\rangle\ge0$ on $K$. If $(y,t)$ is within $\varepsilon$ of $K$, Cauchy–Schwarz gives $t\ge h(y)-\varepsilon\|(-p,1)\|\ge h(y)-3R\varepsilon/r$. This proves the IN implication, also at the transverse-ball boundary by the bound from step 2.1 on slightly larger balls and passage to its limit. [F1, F5, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]
source_lines.63: 5.1 Maintain endpoints $\ell,u$. Initially $\ell=-R\le h(y)+2\delta/3$ and $u=-r/2\ge h(y)-\delta$. An IN answer replaces $u$ by the midpoint and preserves its lower bound by step 4.1; OUT replaces $\ell$ and preserves its upper bound by step 2.2. When $u-\ell\le\delta/3$, these invariants give $h(y)-\delta\le u\le h(y)+\delta$. Each iteration halves the bracket, proving the logarithmic query count. Fixed finite arithmetic and the deterministic oracle completion make the whole binary-search transcript a function of the input label. Store its transcript, copy its output, and reverse its computation and oracle calls; this implements that value oracle with clean work and only a constant factor more queries. [F1, step 4.1, step 2.2, construct, algebra]
